Definition: Baal-Meon, a place East of the Jordan
BiblicalUsage: Baal-meon was a town east of Jordan, in the land of Reuben — given to the Reubenites and rebuilt with a new name, then named again by Ezekiel among the cities of Moab to be judged. Chronicles says the Reubenites dwelt from Aroer to Baal-meon, and Numbers says it was rebuilt as a city of the children of Reuben.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the towns east of Jordan show the cost of settling short of the promise: Reuben kept Baal-meon, and Moab took it back in the end.
